accepted.s: The Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara derived its name from which place?
accepted.x: The dynasty was named after Araviti, also called Aravidu, a village in Kurnool district.
accepted.tq: Use the place-name clue to distinguish the dynasty from similarly named ruling houses.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Aravidu dynasty:
1. It ruled the Vijayanagara Empire from 1570 to 1680.
2. It had seven rulers.
3. It was the first dynasty to rule Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Aravidu dynasty ruled from 1570 to 1680 and had seven rulers. Statement 3 is false because it was the fourth ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara.
accepted.tq: Split the statements and reject the extreme historical claim about being the first dynasty.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s: Who founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570?
accepted.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570.
accepted.tq: Match the founder with his accession place and year.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ramadeva ruled from 1616 to 1630, not from 1600 to 1616. The other pairs correctly give the reign periods stated for those rulers.
accepted.tq: Check the reign-period range rather than relying only on the ruler’s name.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s: Venkatapati Raya II is known in Vijayanagara history by which title?
accepted.x: Venkatapati Raya II, the greatest and longest-ruling Aravidu ruler, was called the Second Krishnadevaraya.
accepted.tq: Use the title-based identification of a ruler.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 is important primarily because it provides information about the genealogy of which dynasties?
accepted.x: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 gives the genealogy of the Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties.
accepted.tq: Identify the inscription through its specific genealogical content.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s: The Battle of Toppur, regarded as the ‘second Talikota’, was fought in which year?
accepted.x: The Battle of Toppur was fought in 1616 and is described as the second Talikota. Jagga Raya was killed in this battle.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive epithet to anchor the associated year.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s: Who was killed in the Battle of Toppur in 1616?
accepted.x: Jagga Raya was killed in the Battle of Toppur in 1616.
accepted.tq: Link the named casualty to the battle rather than confusing him with a later commander.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s:
Arrange the following capitals of the Vijayanagara Empire under the Aravidu rulers in chronological order of their use:
A. Vellore
B. Penukonda
C. Chandragiri

Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: Penukonda was the capital from 1570, followed by Chandragiri, and then Vellore in 1600.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last capitals, then place the intermediate capital.
accepted.sec: Capital shifts after Talikota

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the capital–ruler association after the Battle of Talikota?
o: Penukonda — Tirumala; Chandragiri — Venkatapati II; Vellore — Venkatapati II
Penukonda — Venkatapati II; Chandragiri — Tirumala; Vellore — Sriranga III
Penukonda — Sriranga I; Chandragiri — Ramadeva; Vellore — Tirumala
Penukonda — Ramadeva; Chandragiri — Sriranga II; Vellore — Venkatapati III
accepted.x: Tirumala used Penukonda, while Venkatapati II shifted the capital first to Chandragiri and then to Vellore in 1600.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure capital–ruler pair and verify the remaining sequence.
accepted.sec: Capital shifts after Talikota

accepted.s: Which of the following architectural features spread across Andhra through the Nayaka courts of places such as Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Chandragiri and Vinukonda?
o: Raya gopurams, kalyana mandapas and pillared corridors
accepted.x: Nayaka courts helped spread raya gopurams, kalyana mandapas and pillared corridors across Andhra.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the listed architectural vocabulary from features of other traditions.
accepted.sec: Legacy - temple architecture, Telugu literature, administration models

accepted.s: Who wrote the work Vasucharitra during the Aravidu era?
accepted.x: Ramaraja Bhushanudu authored Vasucharitra, which was dedicated to Tirumala.
accepted.tq: Apply the author–work association without swapping the court figures.
accepted.sec: Legacy - temple architecture, Telugu literature, administration models

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Classical Telugu literature reached its zenith under Krishnadevaraya.
2. Shaivarka Mani Dipika was written by Appayya Dikshita.
3. Vasucharitra was associated with Ramaraja Bhushanudu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Krishnadevaraya’s reign marked the zenith of classical Telugu, while Appayya Dikshita and Ramaraja Bhushanudu are linked with the two named works.
accepted.tq: Verify each author–work and period association before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Legacy - temple architecture, Telugu literature, administration models

accepted.s: The Nayankara or Amaranayaka system is chiefly associated with which aspect of Vijayanagara administration?
o: Land and military assignments to local chiefs
Election of provincial governors by temple assemblies
Appointment of village priests by the emperor
accepted.x: The Nayankara or Amaranayaka system involved the assignment of territories and responsibilities to military-local chiefs. After 1565, many nayakas became hereditary local rulers.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative institution from its practical role in governance.
accepted.sec: Legacy - temple architecture, Telugu literature, administration models

accepted.s: After the weakening of the Vijayanagara Empire, the amara-nayakas developed into which group?
o: Hereditary Palegars and the forerunners of zamindars
accepted.x: The amara-nayakas became hereditary Palegars, who were forerunners of the zamindars.
accepted.tq: Trace the institutional transformation after imperial decline.
accepted.sec: Andhra Nayakas and Palegars after Talikota

accepted.s: Who surveyed and mapped the ruins of Hampi in 1800?
accepted.x: Colin Mackenzie surveyed and mapped the Hampi ruins in 1800 and later became the first Surveyor General of India.
accepted.tq: Associate the survey date with the correct investigator.
accepted.sec: Rediscovery and survey of Hampi - who, when

accepted.s: Which work brought the history of Vijayanagara to wide notice in 1900?
o: The History of the Bahmani Kingdom
accepted.x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire, published in 1900, brought Vijayanagara history to wide notice.
accepted.tq: Use the title–author–year combination to avoid confusing later historical works.
accepted.sec: Rediscovery and survey of Hampi - who, when

accepted.s: Venkatapati Raya II ruled the Aravidu dynasty during which period?
accepted.x: Venkatapati Raya II ruled from 1585 to 1614, a period of 29 years.
accepted.tq: Use the middle reign-period option and verify the start and end years.
accepted.sec: Venkatapati Raya II (1585-1614) - capitals, Europeans, missionaries

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a feature of Venkatapati Raya II’s foreign policy?
o: He accepted Akbar’s demand for submission and severed relations with Europe.
He rejected Akbar’s demand, maintained ties with Portugal and Philip II of Spain, and allowed the Dutch to establish a factory at Pulicat.
He expelled all European traders from the east coast.
He transferred Pulicat to the Golconda Sultanate.
accepted.x: Venkatapati II rejected Akbar’s demand for submission, maintained relations with the Portuguese and Philip II of Spain, and permitted the Dutch factory at Pulicat.
accepted.tq: Separate the ruler’s multiple diplomatic actions from absolute reversal statements.
accepted.sec: Venkatapati Raya II (1585-1614) - capitals, Europeans, missionaries

accepted.s: At which places did Venkatapati Raya II permit the Jesuits to build churches?
accepted.x: Venkatapati II allowed the Jesuits to build churches at Chandragiri and Nellore.
accepted.tq: Pair the ruler with the precise locations connected to missionary activity.
accepted.sec: Venkatapati Raya II (1585-1614) - capitals, Europeans, missionaries

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Venkatapati Raya II is correct?
1. He was called the Second Andhra Bhoja.
2. Appayya Dikshita was associated with his court.
3. His coins bore the inscription ‘Om Venkateshwaraya Namah’.
4. He defeated Veerappa Nayaka of Madurai at Vallankota.
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe Venkatapati Raya II, his court, coinage and military success at Vallankota.
accepted.tq: Check each closely connected biographical detail before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Venkatapati Raya II (1585-1614) - capitals, Europeans, missionaries

accepted.s: The villages granted by Venkatapati Raya II were associated with which Muslim saint?
accepted.x: Venkatapati II gave villages to the Muslim saint Babanathu, as recorded in the Penukonda inscription.
accepted.tq: Use the specific inscriptional association to identify the correct saint.
accepted.sec: Venkatapati Raya II (1585-1614) - capitals, Europeans, missionaries

accepted.s: Rama Raya was the de facto ruler of Vijayanagara while serving as regent for which nominal king?
accepted.x: Aliya Rama Raya ruled as regent for the nominal king Sadasiva Raya from 1543 onward.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the nominal sovereign from the actual power-holder.
accepted.sec: Rama Raya - regency and policy toward the Deccan Sultans

accepted.s: Which policy best describes Rama Raya’s approach towards the Deccan Sultans?
o: He formed a permanent confederacy with all the Sultans against Golconda.
He accepted the supremacy of Ahmadnagar in all Deccan affairs.
He played the Sultans against one another to advance Vijayanagara interests.
He maintained permanent neutrality and avoided all alliances.
accepted.x: Rama Raya exploited rivalries among the Deccan Sultans, supporting different states at different times for Vijayanagara’s advantage.
accepted.tq: Identify the governing strategy from the sequence of changing alliances.
accepted.sec: Rama Raya - regency and policy toward the Deccan Sultans

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Rama Raya’s Deccan policy:
1. In 1546–47, he supported Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar.
2. He acquired the Raichur doab during that phase.
3. From 1557 to 1563, he supported Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe Rama Raya’s shifting alliances and territorial policy in the Deccan.
accepted.tq: Track the dates and changing allies carefully; the reversal of alliances is the key trap.
accepted.sec: Rama Raya - regency and policy toward the Deccan Sultans

accepted.s: What was the Turka Vada established by Rama Raya?
accepted.x: Rama Raya established a Muslim quarter known as the Turka Vada.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a place-name and administrative or military terminology.
accepted.sec: Rama Raya - regency and policy toward the Deccan Sultans

accepted.s: Who was the guru of Rama Raya?
accepted.x: Tatacharya was the guru of Rama Raya.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler with the associated religious teacher.
accepted.sec: Rama Raya - regency and policy toward the Deccan Sultans

accepted.s: Who arranged the grant associated with Madras during the post-Talikota period?
accepted.x: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka, the Kalahasti-Wandiwash chief, arranged the Madras grant.
accepted.tq: Use the office and place association to identify the responsible Nayaka.
accepted.sec: Andhra Nayakas and Palegars after Talikota

accepted.s: Which pair of leaders won the Battle of Toppur in 1616?
o: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore
Mir Jumla and Sriranga Raya III
Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka and Veerappa Nayaka
accepted.x: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore won the Battle of Toppur in 1616.
accepted.tq: Start with the battle year and match the associated victorious commanders.
accepted.sec: Andhra Nayakas and Palegars after Talikota

accepted.s: At Gandikota in 1657, who is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon?
accepted.x: Mir Jumla of Golconda is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon at Gandikota in 1657.
accepted.tq: Link the place and year with the named military commander.
accepted.sec: Andhra Nayakas and Palegars after Talikota

accepted.s: A 1605 inscription at Siddhavatam fort in Kadapa records which event?
o: Mir Jumla melting temple idols into cannon
Tirumala Raya being crowned as founder of the dynasty
Matli Ananta building the fort walls under Venkatapati II
Rama Raya establishing the Turka Vada
accepted.x: The 1605 Siddhavatam inscription records that Matli Ananta built the fort walls during the reign of Venkatapati II.
accepted.tq: Use the inscription’s date and location to identify the recorded construction activity.
accepted.sec: Andhra Nayakas and Palegars after Talikota

accepted.s: Who was the last ruler of the Aravidu dynasty?
accepted.x: Sriranga Raya III was the last Aravidu ruler. He was defeated at Vandavasi in 1642 and died in 1680, marking the end of the empire.
accepted.tq: Identify the final ruler through the succession sequence and terminal date.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals

accepted.s: Sriranga Raya III was defeated at Vandavasi in 1642 by whom?
accepted.x: Mir Jumla of Golconda defeated Sriranga Raya III at Vandavasi in 1642.
accepted.tq: Avoid the ruler–commander swap by matching the battle with its victor.
accepted.sec: Aravidu dynasty - rulers and shifting capitals
